clue.text: Amateur criminal runs gambling scheme

definitions.meaning: A. J. ..., E. W. Hornung's gentleman burglar, is called the amateur cracksman
to run a lottery for prizes, third-person singular verb

explanation.surface: A gentleman thief turns to organising illegal betting.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Raffles is the cricket-playing gentleman thief of E. W. Hornung's stories, billed as 'the amateur cracksman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a fictional burglar's name; the second is the verb for selling tickets in a prize draw.

clue.text: Unguarded spots

definitions.meaning: an outbreak of red marks on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are ordinary synonyms: reckless behaviour, and a skin eruption.

clue.text: Reasonable message in general for Parliament

parts.note: reasonable means fair, just
a fax is a message sent by telephone line

explanation.surface: A sensible note arrives from a commander serving the parliamentary side.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Fairfax commanded Parliament's New Model Army in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Fairfax led the parliamentary forces against Charles I, so he is a general who fought for Parliament.

clue.text: Chapter-house?

parts.note: a chapter is a local branch of a society, and the building where Freemasons' or similar branches meet is the place meant

explanation.definitionFit: A Masonic or fraternal branch and its meeting place share this name, as a chapter does.

clue.text: Channel's depth is a problem

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in a muddle, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors complain that the waterway is too shallow or too deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DEPTH IS A are shuffled; the definition's 's is read as 'is', linking it to the wordplay. Spithead is the strait between Portsmouth and the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: This stretch of sea off Portsmouth, an anchorage for the Royal Navy, is a channel of the Solent.

clue.text: Motorway that is wide in the middle of Us region

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: says the letter for wide sits inside the Latin phrase

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A broad road runs through the heart of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is the United States; the capital is hidden by its position at the start of 'Us region'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midwest is a large area of the central northern United States.

clue.text: Foreign character getting on top of insignificant action by rebels

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
insignificant means tiny

explanation.surface: An outsider takes control of a trivial protest by insurgents.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt against authority, especially by sailors or soldiers, is rebellious action.

clue.text: Missile target offering opportunities for multiple success

definitions.text: Missile target offering opportunities for multiple success

parts.words: Missile target offering opportunities for multiple success
parts.note: the missile is a dart, and the target has rings for doubles and trebles, scoring a multiple of a number

explanation.definitionFit: A pub game's target has double and treble rings, so one throw can score several times its number.

clue.text: Feat of former pilot-look, getting higher than!

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving a piece higher means moving it earlier in the word

parts.note: taken as the word itself
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: An old aviator boasts of a stunt, gazing down from above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting higher than' moves LO above the I of PILOT, giving PLOIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring deed, a heroic achievement.

clue.text: Currently overwhelmed, take steps to keep one's head up

definitions.text: Currently overwhelmed, take steps to keep one's head up

parts.words: Currently overwhelmed, take steps to keep one's head up
parts.note: a swimmer swamped by a current moves the legs as if walking to stay afloat

explanation.definitionFit: Treading, moving the legs upright in deep liquid, keeps a swimmer afloat; figuratively it means just staying in place.

clue.text: Drops flying, meaning to go on car ride

indicators.note: the piece for meaning is added after the one for car ride

parts.note: a spin is a short drive for pleasure
the drift of a remark is its meaning

explanation.surface: An argument about whether to take a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops flying' means droplets carried through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindrift is spray blown from the crests of waves, water droplets carried by wind.

clue.text: India's ready to take nothing from Europe, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged in some other way

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: India declines to accept any money from European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O from EUROPE, leaving EURPE, and rearrange. 'The ready' is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is India's currency, its ready money.

clue.text: Family Shylock couldn't get together

definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice Shylock may take a pound of meat but no drop of the red fluid, so he cannot have both

explanation.definitionFit: Relatives are one's own kin; Portia's ruling separates the body tissue from the blood.

clue.text: Support head's position

parts.note: a stand is a support or base
a point is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: A pedestal shows where the bust sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is a viewpoint, an attitude or position from which things are judged.

clue.text: Excise allowance, bringing strain to holiday

parts.note: to tax is to strain, as in taxing one's patience
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A duty concession eases the pressure when going away.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax break is a concession reducing tax owed, an allowance against duty.

clue.text: It shows highs and lows putting end to investment girl set up

parts.note: investment is an old word for a siege, and relief ends a siege

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A financier sets up a young woman after giving up investing.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of chart shows hills and valleys by shading or moulding, depicting the land's heights and depressions.

clue.text: Chap taking endless gin as an aid to meditation

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for gin is cut off

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: A man drinks gin to help him meditate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or sound repeated to focus the mind during meditation.

clue.text: Knight using weapon a good deal

parts.note: a lance is a long spear
a lot means a good deal, much

explanation.surface: A knight in armour carries a spear and fights often.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot is the Round Table knight of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Complaint Lord rejected, seizing what's originally Greek

indicators.note: seizing says the reversed peer's name holds the initial
rejected means the peer's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon marbles to Britain

indicators.note: originally signals the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A peer dismisses a grumble about the Greek marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ELGIN into NIGLE, which takes G from 'Greek'. The surface plays on the Elgin Marbles dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggle is a minor complaint or nagging worry.

clue.text: Turn stream of water on a big bruiser

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A hose is turned on a large thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla is slang for a big heavy thug, like the great ape.

clue.text: Source of narcotic buccaneer found on island

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means placed after

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan privateer

explanation.surface: A pirate is found on an island growing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake plant has a root yielding a narcotic and was used as a sedative.

clue.text: Such reasoning excellent to trap religious leader

indicators.note: the two letters for excellent enclose the abbot's deputy

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here with I for 1
a prior heads a priory

explanation.surface: Logic devised to catch a church leader out.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from principles to consequences, without experience.

clue.text: Express runner, say, tired out, inhaling oxygen

indicators.note: inhaling means the shuffled letters take in the gas symbol
out signals rearrangement, letters thrown out of order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A tired athlete in a fast race gasps for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TIRED to EDITR, and 'inhaling' puts O inside. The Express is a British newspaper, not a fast runner.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of a newspaper such as the Daily Express runs it.

clue.text: Normal style of building

definitions.meaning: in geometry a normal is a line at right angles to a surface
the late English Gothic architectural style

explanation.definitionFit: A normal is a line at a right angle; and late Gothic church architecture in England bears this name.

clue.text: Some Europeans decline to speak

indicators.note: to speak signals that the word for decline is heard rather than read

parts.note: a lapse is a decline, a falling off

explanation.surface: Some foreigners refuse to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lapps or Sami are the indigenous people of northern Scandinavia.

clue.text: See below river bank

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece for See sits underneath

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, such as Ely

explanation.surface: Look down at the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on them.

clue.text: Faith the continental put in ideology

indicators.note: put in means the French article is placed inside the doctrine

parts.note: an ism is a doctrine or ideology
la is French for the, a continental language

explanation.surface: Religion that a European brings into his belief system.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the religion of Muslims.

clue.text: Get ring here, perhaps, then elope in confusion

indicators.note: in confusion signals that the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man buys a ring, then panics and runs off with his love.
explanation.definitionFit: One receives a call on a phone line, so the device is where one gets a ring.

clue.text: Man who deals with coats rejects theatre role

indicators.note: rejects means the run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: rep is a repertory theatre
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A costume man turns down a part in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapper catches animals for their furs, so he deals in pelts.

clue.text: Irritable if called in to bear witness

indicators.note: called in says the word if is placed inside

parts.note: testy means irritable

explanation.surface: A grumpy witness is summoned to give evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence in court.
